story_description: Build the foundational infrastructure for displaying interactive tutorial overlays that highlight UI elements and guide users through the application with tooltips and spotlights.
task: E005-F003-S002-T001: Implement Tutorial Overlay Core Components
task_description: Create the core SwiftUI components for the tutorial system including TutorialTarget enum, TutorialViewModel, TutorialOverlayView, TutorialBackdrop, TutorialCallout, and TutorialAnchorPreferenceKey.
atom_description: Implement the complete tutorial overlay infrastructure consisting of seven tutorial targets (New Session, Worktree Sidebar, File Tree, Terminal Panel, Chat Area, Chat Input, Right Sidebar), a view model for state management, overlay view for rendering, backdrop for dimming, callout for tooltips, and preference key for anchor positioning.
problem_statement: New users launching Blaze for the first time have no guided introduction to the application's features. The three-pane layout with sessions, chat, and sidebar contains numerous interactive elements that are not self-discoverable. Without a tutorial system, users may miss key features like worktree management, hook configuration, and timeline visualization.
scope_in: TutorialTarget enum defining 7 anchored regions: newSession, worktreeSidebar, fileTree, terminalPanel, chatArea, chatInput, rightSidebar
TutorialViewModel ObservableObject managing currentStep, isActive, progress calculations, and step navigation
TutorialOverlayView SwiftUI view composing backdrop and callout based on current target
TutorialBackdrop view rendering semi-transparent overlay with spotlight cutout using GeometryReader
TutorialCallout view displaying tooltip with title, description, step indicator, and navigation buttons
TutorialAnchorPreferenceKey for collecting anchor bounds from tutorial-enabled views
TutorialAnchorModifier view modifier for marking views as tutorial targets
scope_out: Individual tutorial step content and copy (separate atoms O010-O016)
App-level integration into BlazeApp.swift (separate atom O017-INTEGRATE)
Animation polish and accessibility motion settings (separate atom O018-POLISH)
Persistence of tutorial completion state to UserDefaults
Skip tutorial functionality and confirmation dialog
assumptions: SwiftUI preference keys are the appropriate mechanism for collecting anchor bounds across the view hierarchy
GeometryReader will provide accurate frame measurements for spotlight positioning
The tutorial will run as an overlay on top of ContentView, not as a sheet or full-screen cover
Tutorial targets correspond to existing UI elements that will have stable view identifiers
The tutorial will progress linearly through steps without branching or conditional paths
constraints: Must use SwiftUI-native approaches without UIKit bridging for overlay rendering
Backdrop must dim the entire window except the spotlight cutout area
Callout positioning must avoid clipping at window edges
Tutorial state must be isolated from main application state to prevent side effects
All views must support both light and dark color schemes
Must work correctly with macOS window resizing and full-screen modes

FR-002: Each TutorialTarget provides a computed title property returning a localized string
FR-003: Each TutorialTarget provides a computed description property returning tutorial copy
FR-004: TutorialViewModel publishes currentStep as Int starting at 0
FR-005: TutorialViewModel publishes isActive as Bool controlling overlay visibility
FR-006: TutorialViewModel provides nextStep() method incrementing currentStep with bounds checking
FR-007: TutorialViewModel provides previousStep() method decrementing currentStep with bounds checking
FR-008: TutorialViewModel provides skipTutorial() method setting isActive to false
FR-009: TutorialViewModel provides currentTarget computed property mapping step index to TutorialTarget
FR-010: TutorialOverlayView renders TutorialBackdrop when isActive is true
FR-011: TutorialOverlayView renders TutorialCallout positioned relative to current target anchor
FR-012: TutorialBackdrop renders a full-window Color.black.opacity(0.6) layer
FR-013: TutorialBackdrop cuts out a spotlight rectangle at the target anchor bounds with 8pt padding
FR-014: TutorialCallout displays target title in 16pt semibold font
FR-015: TutorialCallout displays target description in 14pt regular font with 60% opacity
FR-016: TutorialCallout displays step indicator as 'Step N of 7' text
FR-017: TutorialCallout provides Previous button disabled on first step
FR-018: TutorialCallout provides Next button with 'Finish' label on last step
FR-019: TutorialAnchorPreferenceKey collects CGRect values keyed by TutorialTarget
FR-020: tutorialAnchor(for:) view modifier applies preference key to any SwiftUI view
nonfunctional_requirements: NFR-001: Tutorial overlay must render at 60fps without frame drops during step transitions
NFR-002: Memory footprint of tutorial system must not exceed 5MB when active
NFR-003: Tutorial components must be fully accessible via VoiceOver with proper labels
NFR-004: Callout text must maintain WCAG AA contrast ratio (4.5:1) against backdrop
NFR-005: Tutorial must handle window resize events within 16ms without visual glitches
implementation_steps: Step 2: Define TutorialTarget enum in TutorialTarget.swift with 7 cases and computed title/description properties
Step 3: Implement TutorialAnchorPreferenceKey in TutorialAnchorPreferenceKey.swift as PreferenceKey with CGRect values
Step 4: Create tutorialAnchor(for:) ViewModifier in TutorialAnchorPreferenceKey.swift
Step 5: Implement TutorialViewModel in TutorialViewModel.swift as ObservableObject with @Published properties
Step 6: Add step navigation methods (nextStep, previousStep, skipTutorial) to TutorialViewModel
Step 7: Implement TutorialBackdrop in TutorialBackdrop.swift using Canvas or Shape for spotlight cutout
Step 8: Implement TutorialCallout in TutorialCallout.swift with title, description, step indicator, and buttons
Step 9: Create TutorialOverlayView in TutorialOverlayView.swift composing backdrop and callout
Step 10: Add preference key observer in TutorialOverlayView using onPreferenceChange
Step 11: Implement callout positioning logic to keep callout within window bounds
Step 12: Add @EnvironmentObject injection point for TutorialViewModel in TutorialOverlayView
Step 13: Write unit tests for TutorialViewModel state transitions
Step 14: Write UI tests for callout positioning edge cases
data_model_changes: TutorialTarget enum: newSession, worktreeSidebar, fileTree, terminalPanel, chatArea, chatInput, rightSidebar
TutorialAnchorPreferenceKey.Value: [TutorialTarget: CGRect] dictionary mapping targets to frame bounds
api_contracts: TutorialViewModel.nextStep() -> Void: Increments currentStep if currentStep < 6, otherwise sets isActive to false
TutorialViewModel.previousStep() -> Void: Decrements currentStep if currentStep > 0
TutorialViewModel.skipTutorial() -> Void: Sets isActive to false immediately
TutorialViewModel.startTutorial() -> Void: Sets currentStep to 0 and isActive to true
TutorialViewModel.currentTarget: TutorialTarget? computed property returning TutorialTarget.allCases[currentStep] or nil
tutorialAnchor(for: TutorialTarget) -> some ViewModifier: Returns modifier that reports bounds via preference key
event_contracts: TutorialStepChanged: Published when currentStep changes, payload includes previousStep and newStep integers
TutorialCompleted: Published when user reaches final step and taps Finish button
TutorialSkipped: Published when user taps Skip button at any step
TutorialStarted: Published when startTutorial() is called
ui_states: Inactive: Tutorial overlay not visible, TutorialViewModel.isActive is false
Active Step N: Overlay visible with spotlight on target N, callout showing step N content
Transitioning: Brief state during step animation, spotlight and callout animating to new positions
Completing: Final step with Finish button visible, about to dismiss
ui_interactions: Tap Next button: Advances to next tutorial step or completes tutorial on final step
Tap Previous button: Returns to previous tutorial step, disabled on first step
Tap Skip button: Dismisses tutorial immediately without completing
Tap outside callout: No action, tutorial remains active until explicitly dismissed
Window resize: Anchors recalculate, spotlight and callout reposition accordingly
ui_copy: Step 1 Description: Create a new coding session to get started with your AI assistant.
Step 2 Description: Manage multiple worktrees and switch between different projects.
Step 3 Description: Browse and open files from your project directory.
Step 4 Description: View command output and interact with your shell.
Step 5 Description: See your conversation history with the AI assistant.
Step 6 Description: Type your prompts and questions here.
Step 7 Description: Access Timeline, Tools, Tasks, Token usage, and Hook configuration.
edge_cases: EC-001: Window resized smaller than callout minimum width (280pt) - callout should scroll or truncate gracefully
EC-002: Tutorial target view not in hierarchy (e.g., sidebar collapsed) - skip that step or show centered callout with instruction to expand
EC-003: Multiple windows open - tutorial should only appear in frontmost window
EC-004: App enters background during tutorial - pause tutorial state, resume on foreground
EC-005: User rapidly taps Next multiple times - debounce navigation to prevent step skipping
EC-006: Accessibility large text enabled - callout must expand to accommodate larger fonts
EC-007: Right-to-left language layout - callout positioning must flip appropriately
failure_modes: FM-001: Preference key returns empty dictionary - fallback to centered overlay without spotlight
FM-002: TutorialViewModel not injected into environment - fatal error with descriptive message in debug, silent skip in release
FM-003: Anchor bounds return zero rect - treat as missing target, show generic positioning
FM-004: Animation interrupted by state change - cancel in-flight animations cleanly
FM-005: Memory pressure during tutorial - tutorial system should be first to release resources
rollback_plan: To rollback tutorial infrastructure: 1) Delete Blaze/Sources/Tutorial/ directory entirely, 2) Remove any tutorialAnchor modifiers from ContentView and child views, 3) Remove TutorialViewModel @EnvironmentObject from BlazeApp, 4) Remove TutorialOverlayView overlay from ContentView. No data migrations required as tutorial state is ephemeral.

TutorialOverlayIntegrationTests.testBackdropRendersWhenActive: Verify backdrop appears when isActive is true
TutorialOverlayIntegrationTests.testCalloutPositioning: Verify callout positions near anchor bounds

tutorial.skipped: Fired when user skips, properties: {skipped_at_step, timestamp}

metrics.target: Average step duration under 10 seconds indicates good pacing

metrics.name: tutorial_overlay_render_time
metrics.notes: Measure using Instruments Time Profiler on overlay draw

[Tutorial] Advanced to step N (target: targetName) - logged on each nextStep() call

open_questions: Should tutorial auto-advance after a timeout if user does not interact?
Should tutorial show on every fresh install or only on first-time app launch?
How should tutorial behave if a target view is hidden (e.g., collapsed sidebar)?
notes: This atom provides the infrastructure only. Individual step content is defined in separate atoms O010-O016. App integration is handled in O017-INTEGRATE. Animation polish is in O018-POLISH.
verification_steps: Run xcodebuild test -scheme Blaze -only-testing:BlazeTests/TutorialViewModelTests and verify all tests pass
Open Blaze/Sources/Tutorial/TutorialOverlayView.swift in Xcode, view preview canvas, and verify overlay renders with backdrop and callout

risks: Preference key may not collect anchors from deeply nested views if preference propagation is interrupted
Spotlight cutout rendering may have performance issues with complex window shapes
Callout positioning near window edges may cause clipping on small screens
mitigations: Use onPreferenceChange at TutorialOverlayView level which captures all descendant preferences
Use simple rectangular cutout with rounded corners rather than complex paths
Implement edge detection logic that shifts callout inward when within 20pt of window bounds
risk_register.blast_radius: Tutorial infrastructure is isolated to Blaze/Sources/Tutorial/ directory. Failure would only affect onboarding experience, not core app functionality. Users can still use all app features without tutorial.
risk_register.fallback_plan: If tutorial system has critical bugs, set hasCompletedOnboarding=true by default in BlazeApp to skip tutorial entirely. Users can access help documentation instead.

events: TutorialStepChanged(previousStep: Int, newStep: Int): Published by TutorialViewModel when step changes
TutorialCompleted: Published when user finishes tutorial
TutorialSkipped(atStep: Int): Published when user skips tutorial
persistence: Tutorial state is ephemeral within session - completion persistence handled by O017-INTEGRATE via @AppStorage
